decisions.reason: Turnaround management software has its own website page, is close to the core offer and central to the announced data-driven airport direction, so the firm's visible commitment and investment make dropping it very unlikely.
The apron connectivity module underpins the integrated digital platform strategy, and any slow uptake can be attributed to long airport project cycles, so management persists with it.

Revenue and billing software is less central to airside operations and only mentioned on the website, but it builds on the established offer and has only just been launched, so the firm keeps it for now.
Equipment monitoring supports the firm's expansion into service and lifecycle offerings and draws on its installed base, so it fits the announced direction and stays.
Apron resource management is close to the core offer and integral to the end-to-end operations suite, so the sunk investment and strategic fit favour keeping it.
The controller safety alert service ties into the firm's tower and safety positioning, and adoption in air traffic control is slow by nature, so weak early results are seen as temporary.
